objective: The complexity side of the thesis. Three-place knots carry emergence, but the program has shown that emergence and hardness are distinct notions (Horn and affine knots are easy). Ask where hardness lives: in hub-free networks, where each distinction joins two knots, or in hubs, where a distinction joins three. Nearest known work: Boolean edge constraint problems and delta-matroids (Feder 2001; Kazda, Kolmogorov and Rolinek 2019), the general factor problem (Lovasz 1972; Cornuejols 1988) and Tseitin lower bounds. Standalone value: classify the 34 three-place knots, test whether hub-free networks of every knot are tractable while hubs carry NP-hardness, and find which knots carry resolution hardness without hubs.
status: Complete 2026-10-24: hubs and memory. Native networks of every law are polynomial without external theorems, and every native contradiction, cut at its bridges, is a set of parity systems (half rule); without parity knots contradictions are necklaces of odd wire rings refuted in linear size with two-literal derived clauses, while parity networks on expanders are exponentially hard for resolution; hubs carry NP-hardness (conditional). Next: counting what emerges natively, deferred to the owner.
title: Hubs and memory: the complexity of native knot networks
